transcript:
Meeting header:
[2026-09-05 16:00 PDT] Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Taylor Nguyen (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (NovaHealth CTO), Priya Shah (Head of Platform), Samir Khan (Security Lead), Lena Ortiz (SRE), Chris Boyle (Procurement)

Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on org/project keys, rate limiting, and multi-tenant quotas. Customer trying to understand isolation between teams, enforcement points (API vs console), and options for burst vs guaranteed capacity.

Topics: org vs project keys, per-route rate limits, global quotas, per-project billing/cost controls, SSO & RBAC integration, security/compliance docs, next steps for sandbox and benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, i'll run the quick agenda, jordan's gonna do the deep dive on rate limits and the console.
[00:12] Alex: hey thanks, morning for us, afternoon for you — short intro, our main ask is we need strong multi-tenant controls because we run many internal teams and partners.
[00:22] Priya: yeah we want per-team quotas, and the ability to spin up project keys that only allow embeddings or only allow chat generation, and separate billing.
[00:35] Jordan: (laughs) great, that's exactly what we'll show — org keys, project keys mapping to roles. just a note, i'll probably jump into the console and then show API examples.
[01:00] Taylor: small caveat, transcription may say KV cash at times, it's KV cache — apologies for any auto-transcribe glitches.
[01:20] Samir: security first question, what level of isolation do you provide? like can a project key access other projects' cached KV?
[01:35] Jordan: good call, short answer — no. project keys are scoped to project namespace. KV cache and prefix caching are isolated by project id so cross-project leakage isn't allowed. we also log access per key.
[02:05] Alex: and how about rate limits — per org and per project? we have tenants that spike unpredictably during peak hours.
[02:16] Jordan: we support multilayered limits: global org quota (tokens/month), per-project daily quotas, and per-route rate limits (qps). you can configure burst capacity for projects or reserve dedicated capacity if you need guaranteed throughput.
[02:47] Priya: is burst capacity automatic or configured? we don't want noisy neighbors to cause latencies.
[02:56] Jordan: you control burst size per project and there's an autoscale/burst policy. defaults are conservative, but for production we recommend explicit configs. we also have token-based throttling and leaky-bucket style smoothing.
[03:18] Lena: what's enforcement point? api gateway or client-side?
[03:24] Jordan: enforcement is at the gateway in our control plane for hosted. for private deployments it's enforced by the local control plane component and can integrate with your rate limit proxies.
[03:40] Samir: does that mean if we go private on prem, we still get the same org/project controls?
[03:46] Maya: yes, the control plane surface is the same; the difference is where the control plane runs and whether logs leave your VPC.
[03:56] [05:00] Jordan: ok jumping into the console — starting with org settings, you can see monthly token budget, alerts, and per-project quotas. (screen share noises)
[05:18] Jordan: here we have 'projects' list — each project has API keys, allowed routes (generation, embeddings, rerank), quota windows, and a usage preview.
[05:35] Alex: can we restrict a project to embeddings-only?
[05:39] Jordan: yes, you pick allowed endpoints per key — i can demo creating a key that only has embeddings scope.
[05:48] Taylor: quick demo note: some models may be referred to incorrectly in transcripts — e.g., 'Redwood Verifed' shows as 'redwood verified' in the raw export.
[06:05] Jordan: creating a project key now: name = 'analytics-embeddings', scope = embeddings only, quota = 500k tokens/month, rate limit = 20 rps, burst = 50. shows as active.
[06:30] Priya: can we tie that key to a specific billing center and have separate invoices?
[06:36] Jordan: yes — projects map to billing units; you can export per-project usage and tag cost centers.
[06:45] Samir: audit logs — where do we get the key use logs and for how long are they retained?
[06:52] Jordan: logs are available in the console and via log export to your SIEM for retention. default retention is 90 days for hosted; enterprise add-on gives longer retention. we also provide HMAC-signed delivery to your S3 for archiving.
[07:10] Alex: cool. about quotas: if a project hits quota, what's the behavior? hard fail, soft degrade?
[07:18] Jordan: configurable. you can set hard blocks, soft warnings, or fallback policies to a cheaper model. we have roll-over windows or temporary grace with rate limiting.
[07:31] Priya: fallback to cheaper models is interesting — do you do model family mapping automatically?
[07:38] Jordan: you define fallback model variants per route, for example gpt-like -> smaller quantized variant. policy can be per-org or per-project.
[07:50] [09:00] Alex: we use on-prem data for some requests, will the project keys ever transmit PII to the hosted plane?
[09:08] Maya: if you use hosted, logs leave our control plane — sensitive workloads should use private deployment; we also have options to disable request logging and keep only token counts, or encrypt payloads with customer-managed keys.
[09:28] Samir: that encryption — is it envelope encryption with our KMS?
[09:33] Jordan: yes, integrates with CMKs in AWS KMS and HSM options for private. also supports encrypt-at-rest and in-transit.
[09:45] Lena: latency question — rate limiting adds latency in the critical path? our SLAs are strict.
[09:51] Jordan: enforcement is a lightweight check at the gateway, typically sub-millisecond. heavier policies like dynamic batching don't add to per-request critical path once warmed.
[10:05] Chris: procurement question — pricing model for per-project quotas vs dedicated capacity?
[10:12] Maya: hosted API is usage based; per-project quotas are billing controls. dedicated/reserved capacity has commitment pricing and predictable throughput. we'll send a pricing appendix.
[10:28] Alex: what's the developer experience — rotating keys, programmatic key creation?
[10:33] Jordan: full API for org management: create project, generate keys, revoke, rotate. also support service principals and short-lived ephemeral tokens for clients.
[10:48] Priya: ephemeral tokens sound helpful for mobile clients. any SDK support?
[10:52] Taylor: yes, SDKs for js/python and examples for token rotation flows.
[11:05] [13:00] Jordan: demoing API call now — using the embeddings-only key, calling /v1/embeddings, success 200, rate-limited test next.
[13:20] Jordan: simulating a burst of 100 rps — observe throttling to 20 rps configured — 429 responses for excess and headers return x-rate-limit-remaining and reset. some transcripts may show headers slightly wrong (x-rate-limit-remain, etc.)
[13:45] Alex: can we change response to queue instead of 429?
[13:50] Jordan: we don't queue in hosted — we return 429; for dedicated there's an option to front with your queueing proxy or we can support delayed batching depending on architecture.
[14:10] Samir: how do we onboard multiple internal teams? we have 30+ squads.
[14:16] Maya: recommended pattern — org owner creates projects per team, seed keys with ephemeral rotation via CI, apply per-project budgets, and set alerts. we can help with templates.
[14:30] Priya: can projects be nested or inherit policies?
[14:35] Jordan: we have policy inheritance at org-level; projects inherit unless overridden. no deep nesting but you can do tag/grouping.
[14:50] [17:00] Jordan: show console alerts — threshold alerts for usage, percent-of-budget, and rate limit alerts. can route alerts to slack/webhooks.
[17:16] Alex: wanted confirmation on RBAC: can we restrict who can create project keys?
[17:22] Jordan: yes RBAC roles: org admin, billing, project admin, key manager, viewer. you can enforce SSO + SCIM provisioning.
[17:36] Samir: SCIM for automating roles? good. do you have audit export for role changes?
[17:42] Jordan: yep full audit trail for role changes with timestamps and actor principal.
[17:50] Lena: about metrics — can we get per-key latency histograms to trace regressions?
[17:57] Jordan: yes per-key/per-route latency and token cost metrics; console shows p50/p95/p99 and traces link to full request logs.
[18:15] Priya: wondering about cross-project cost controls: can we enforce hard cost caps and auto-disable keys?
[18:22] Jordan: yes you can set hard cost caps that will auto-disable keys once reached or put into grace mode and trigger notifications.
[18:35] [20:00] Alex: anything to call out on security checklist for enterprise?
[20:05] Maya: we'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts; for private deployments we provide network diagram and support for your SIEM; single-tenant dedicated pools available if you need physical separation.
[20:20] Samir: can logging be scrubbed for PII before export?
[20:25] Jordan: we have redaction hooks and pre-send processors; for private installs you can run redaction locally.
[20:40] Priya: we need to run a benchmark — emulate our traffic pattern: mix of generation + embeddings, spikes to 400 rps for certain jobs. can you support a controlled run?
[20:53] Jordan: yes we'll run a benchmark in sandbox; need input traffic shape and sample prompts.
[21:07] Maya: next steps recap — we'll send pricing + SLA docs, security pack, provision sandbox org with project keys, and schedule benchmark.
[21:20] Chris: procurement follow-up — what's the procurement timeline? we usually need 4-6 weeks.
[21:26] Maya: noted, we'll align trial to your procurement cadence; Jordan will run the benchmark in parallel.
[21:40] [23:00] Alex: any competitor pitfalls we should watch? we've looked at openai and bedrock — main concerns are multi-tenant cost tracking and per-team keys.
[23:11] Maya: yes some vendors have less granular billing per key; we emphasize per-project billing and cost-center tagging.
[23:25] Priya: small nit: demo console latency felt a bit slow on screen share, is that expected?
[23:31] Jordan: UI may lag over screen share; backend calls are separate. production console is faster; we'll share the latency numbers.
[23:45] Samir: can you also include the retention SLA in the docs?
[23:49] Maya: yes, adding to next steps.
[24:00] Jordan: last quick thing — when a project is over quota we can optionally reroute requests to a low-cost cached variant to preserve availability.
[24:12] Alex: that sounds useful.
[24:20] Priya: do you have rate limiting at model route and token level simultaneously?
[24:26] Jordan: yes, both enforced; token-level accounting is separate from request qps.
[24:38] [28:00] Maya: ok wrapping up — recap of owners: maya pricing and SLA by tuesday, jordan sandbox and benchmark, samir provide compliance checks, priya will share team mapping.
[28:20] Alex: thanks everyone.
[28:25] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invites for the benchmark.
[28:35] End of recording — remaining time used for quick procurement clarifications and off-record questions.

Notes: transcript has some auto-transcription artifacts (timestamps gaps, occasional speaker mislabels). key decisions: NovaHealth wants per-project billing + hard cost caps, embeddings-only project keys for analytics, and a benchmark simulating 400 rps spikes.
